Okay, but will dinner still be at 6.30?
Stated my main concern about the dinner time and waiting for a response.

STRATEGY: CLARIFY. Rachel's worried about the time, but I'm worried about having to cook more. If Xin Yi isn't cooking her night, that's a problem for me. I need to get straight to what this means for the rest of us.

Waiting for Xin Yi to explain what the new arrangement would be.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. Marcus asked for a proposal and is worried they'll have to cook more. I need to reassure him and suggest a plan that doesn't burden anyone. My idea is that I still cook for everyone on my night, but a vegetarian meal. On their nights, I'll cook my own food separately. This way, they don't have to change their habits, the schedule stays the same, and we can all still eat together, which is what I want.

No, you wouldn't have to cook more. I can still cook for everyone on my night, it'll just be vegetarian. On your nights, you cook as usual, and I'll just make something separate for myself. We can still eat at the same time.
I've made a proposal and am waiting for their response.

STRATEGY: ACCEPT. Xin Yi's proposal directly addresses my concern. I don't have to cook more than my one night. She'll still cook on her night, it'll just be vegetarian for everyone. And on the other nights, she'll handle her own food. That's fair enough. It doesn't create any extra work for me.
Okay, that works for me.
My main concern has been addressed, so I have nothing more to add right now.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Marcus is okay with Xin Yi's idea, but I'm not. The whole reason I started this rota was so we'd all eat the same meal together. If she's making her own separate food three nights a week, it kind of defeats the purpose. It's not really a shared dinner then. I need to say this.
But then we're not all eating the same thing. The point was to share a meal.
I've explained my objection to Xin Yi's proposal.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Natalie's concern is that we won't really be sharing a meal if we're not eating the same food. I need to address this by explaining my perspective. For me, the important part of sharing is being together at the table, not necessarily eating the exact same dish. I should also remind her that this is a temporary situation, which might make it more acceptable.
I see your point. But we would still all be eating together at the same time. For me, that's the main thing. And it's only for a month.
I've responded to Natalie's concern and am waiting to see if my explanation helps.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Xin Yi thinks eating at the same time is enough, and that a month isn't long. But for me, the whole point of the rota was for us to share the same meal, not just the same table. If she cooks for herself three nights a week, we lose that sense of community I was trying to build. A month is long enough for that habit to break down. I need to explain why sharing the actual food is important to me.
A month is a long time. And if we're not eating the same food, it just feels different. It's not really a shared meal anymore.
I've explained my core objection to her proposal.

STRATEGY: ASSERT. Natalie is focused on us eating the exact same food. For me, the important part of sharing a meal is eating together at the same time. As long as dinner is still at 6.30, I'm okay with Xin Yi's plan. I should state my point of view to help move this along.
For me, the main thing is that we're eating at the same time. As long as it's still 6.30, it works.
I've stated my position, which focuses on the timing.

Okay, so Rachel's fine with it too, as long as the time doesn't change. That's two of us. It's just Natalie who seems to have a problem with it now, about the whole 'sharing a meal' thing. My main concern is solved, I don't have to cook more. So I'll just let them talk it out.
I have nothing to add. My concern has been addressed and I've already agreed to the proposal. The current discussion is between Natalie, Xin Yi, and Rachel.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Rachel's comment is really helpful. It shows that I'm not the only one who thinks eating at the same time is the important part of sharing a meal. I'll agree with Rachel to reinforce the point, making it clear there's another perspective without directly challenging Natalie again.
Yes, that's how I feel too. Being at the table together is what matters.

It's just Natalie who has a problem now. I've made my position clear, there's no need for me to say anything else right now. I'll wait and see what she says.
I've made my point and am waiting for others, particularly Natalie, to respond.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Rachel and Xin Yi have both said that eating at the same time is what matters. They don't see the problem. If we're all eating different things, it undermines the whole reason I started it. I need to explain this core reason, otherwise they won't understand why I'm objecting to what seems like a simple solution to them.
To me, that's not the same. The point was to share a meal, not just a table. If we're all eating different things, we might as well just be cooking for ourselves every night.
I've explained the principle behind my objection. Now I'll wait to see if they understand.

I've made my position clear and have nothing new to add to this part of the discussion.

STRATEGY: CHALLENGE. Natalie is threatening the whole rota system by saying we might as well cook for ourselves every night. That's the opposite of why I agreed to this. I need to push back on that idea immediately because I hate cooking.

I've made my point about the practicalities.

STRATEGY: ACKNOWLEDGE. Marcus is right, the convenience is a huge part of why the rota works. I can't just ignore that. But he's missing my point entirely. It wasn't just about saving work, it was about sharing something. I need to agree with him on the practical side but bring it back to the community aspect that's being lost.
I know. That's a big part of it. But so is eating the same food. Otherwise, we're just... eating in the same room.
I've acknowledged Marcus's point but reiterated my own.

STRATEGY: WITHDRAW. Natalie is just repeating herself now. This argument is going in circles and it doesn't affect my main concern, which is eating at 6.30. I've already said my piece. I don't have anything new to add and I just want this to be settled.
I'm not getting involved in this circular argument.

Natalie is just repeating herself about sharing the same food. I've already made my point that the rota saves a ton of work, and that's what matters to me. Arguing about what counts as a 'real' shared meal is pointless. Xin Yi's plan works. I'm not going to get dragged into a debate about feelings.

I have asked Natalie for her suggestion to resolve the issue.

It's an effort, but it keeps the rota going properly. It's a real compromise.

I've made a counter-proposal. Now I'll wait for their reaction.

STRATEGY: ACCEPT. Natalie's proposal is a generous way to solve her own objection. It keeps the spirit of the shared meal that she cares about. It's a bigger change for everyone than my original idea, but I'm happy to teach them if they're willing to try. I need to make sure Marcus and Rachel are on board before agreeing, since it affects them too.

I've accepted Natalie's proposal contingent on the others agreeing, and now I'm waiting for their response.

I don't mind what we eat. As long as dinner is on the table at 6.30, it's fine with me.
I've stated my condition and am waiting for the others to react.

I'm not learning to cook vegetarian. The first plan was fine.
I've rejected Natalie's proposal and stated my preference.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. Marcus has rejected Natalie's plan for everyone to eat vegetarian. He said my first plan was fine. Rachel doesn't mind either way. This means Natalie's idea won't work for the group. The simplest solution is to go back to my original proposal. I'll suggest that to Natalie, as she's the one who objected to it.
Okay, well, it seems like my first idea might be the easiest for everyone then. You all cook what you want on your nights, and I'll make my own food. We can still eat at the same time.
I have re-proposed my initial idea as the most practical path forward, given Marcus's objection.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Xin Yi is saying her first idea is easiest, but that's the one I already said I don't like. Just because Marcus shot down my suggestion doesn't make her plan okay. The main problem is still there 			we're not eating the same meal. It's not 'easiest for everyone' if it doesn't work for me. I have to stand my ground on this.

I've restated my objection to her original plan.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Natalie is repeating her objection, but her preferred solution was rejected by Marcus. I need to point out this practical constraint. My plan is the only one left that works for everyone, even if it's not perfect for her. I'll frame this as a 'what else can we do?' question to show I'm still trying to solve this together, rather than just defending my idea.

I have explained the impasse and asked Natalie for another suggestion, putting the ball in her court.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. This argument is going in circles. Natalie's idea for everyone to go vegetarian was rejected by Marcus. Xin Yi's original plan works for me and Marcus.
